question: When repeated uses of the same motor primitive control different side effects, can action-only learning transport a newly demonstrated event to the right occurrence on a new world?
status_at_freeze: No event-transfer scores examined. Earlier six-world cohort has known site accuracy and endpoints. Reuse the distinct ten-world teaching cohort for this other outcome; exact-code deduplicated, not a new generator. No fitting.
source: Use all 766 codes in the validated ten-world teaching cohort (SHA256 4fb37ac92f658b4769ad7543d7f613f7373aff4be29b33bb46ac0f6ea5035d90). Decode original program tokens from previously cached HDF5. Verify token hashes and interpreter trajectories on all ten. Training checkpoint seed 17 remains fixed.
assignment: Sort ten indices by SHA256 of event-transfer-v1|code|index. First five are demonstrations. From them list all unordered pairs of distinct executed static sites producing the same primitive, choose the least SHA256 of JSON [code,siteA,siteB] (lexical order by serialized site). If no pair exists omit before examining target executions. Use every remaining world. Evaluate two missions, pulse on the first site versus pulse on the second. Only support traces include a binary pulse aligned to their own observed actions. No cross-world correspondence, site identifiers, program text, or target annotations reach predictors.
endpoint: Shared autonomous support-weighted prefix-edit motor controller for all readouts and both missions. The pulse is a separate output; timestamp on successfully executed actions, no effect on motor dynamics or observations. Require explicit STOP at the correct native grid plus the exact reference list of pulse timestamps for each mission; primary requires success under BOTH mark assignments on the same target. This tests a synthetic transferable side effect, not improvement of the motor policy. Include no-pulse targets. Also report subset where the two reference event streams differ, motor ceiling and per-mission success.
readouts: Given the motor's chosen primitive and the same executed query prefix, predict a pulse iff marked slots have strictly more than half of eligible mass; ties give no pulse. Frozen neural uses learned position probabilities conditional on the chosen action. Simple comparators are equal mass for all occurrences of that action, minimum absolute elapsed-step difference, minimum absolute difference in within-trace previous count of that action, and minimum cost under the frozen support-weighted prefix-edit aligner. The three positional comparators vote uniformly over tied best slots. Include STOP implicitly as no pulse. No tuning or training with marked traces.
primary: Equal-code mean of exact paired-mission success across the five target worlds. Neural minus strongest of the four fixed simple readouts selected again in each of 5000 paired code bootstrap draws (NumPy default_rng 902107). Retain for external exploration only if at least 100 distinct eligible codes, mean gain >= 0.02 and lower 95% endpoint > 0. No retuning or new Karel cohorts if missed. Competing equal-mass readout and oracle motor ceiling secondary. Decision conditional on this single frozen policy and corpus.
budget: One free Frontenac single-CPU Slurm allocation up to ten minutes. No local model or training.
